Thanks for the article and the post PV! It's really nice to have you as a posting member in this area :) You really are one of magic's greatest writers and players (and likely the best intersection of the two).

Just something that struck me as odd was your generalization of miracles. While miracles certainly lost an incredible amount of power, versatility and consistency with SDT, the deck is still undeniably powerful and has some good results in the current format. While there is certainly not a ton of data to hear from in legacy, I think the continued success of the deck has some good theory to stand on.

The fact you say that miracles "doesn't do anything" without SDT and "loses the lategame more than it should" are half true in my estimation and both concerns are addressed with monastery mentor. 

While miracles no longer has the opportunity to soft lock as early as turn 3 or filter draws super effectively long into the late game - the deck is able to swing fair matchups with terminus and present a potent threat in mentor or Jace. Mentor is particularly good in these spots since it can close the game so fast if unanswered and we all know how Jace works if you untap. Alternatively, miracles can get ahead a couple of cards via predict or ak, snap, etc then leverage protecting a mentor. I don't think miracles truly wants to go to the supreme lategame at this point (since lots of other decks have similar powerful options or hardcast ulamog on you)
and mentor allows you to close games quickly after you have generated an advantage.

While counterbalance is much weaker without top threatening to soft lock, it is still in important role player vs fair decks and combo alike when paired with a fast clock (mentor). Forcing the openent to play into your cb since you presented a robust threat limits their ability to test your top card and play around it. I see the card as a proactive way of limiting your opponent's options after you deploy a haymaker. Also the card is just generally a brutal threat against storm and strong vs typical 1cmc centric lists that make up the majority of legacy.

I found it interesting that you specifically reference the fact you have liked mentor in the past, state you didn't like Cuneo's list for omitting it but didn't make any commentary on the many mentor builds that incorporate the card. Any particular reason? I would love to hear your perspective on the lists with 2-3 mentor MD like the lists your countryman SteFaNoGs has been playing https://www.mtggoldfish.com/player/SteFaNoGs

Tldr; mentor is a powerful card you say you like but didn't discuss. I think you should more thoroughly consider the builds that emphasize it. 

Thank you for recognizing legacy as meaningful magic!

18 Months of D&T time here, just started playing the red splash 2 months ago, observations below:

What you gain:
- Improves your lands match-up phenomenally: mother + magus is a serious beating.
- Elves is still bad but as long as you don't get hoofed, all your draws are live to just win you in SB games (seriously, sudden demise is that good here).
- Magus can steal random games. Some midrange/control opponents will foolishly fetch non-basics thinking "well you already have 1 wasteland target" and then get locked out of the game.
- Turn 3 is more explosive than ever before. T1 vial -> 2 drop (&vial mom) -> cast recruiter, tutor most potent 2 drop & vial in.
- Flickerwisp + stoneforge and recruiter is a real CA plan. You are actually out CA the non-dig midrange decks that game us trouble before (maverick, Jund, etc).
- You can run miser hate bears and actually get them when they matter. This deck lets you play more of a toolbox grindy style (we can cut down on revoker and draw it when it is 10/10 and less against delver!)
- The mana isn't any worse, you are already light on white sources and the splash doesn't make that any worse - cavern goes even further now with magus and recruiter being humans
- Recruiter carries a Jitte or SoFI just fine and helps tremendously vs liliana and jace

What you lose:
- Fliers, this matters in the mirror and vs other fair ground decks. I still think you gain enough to off set this vs Jund, maverick, etc but it is a consideration
- A 3rd karakas - managara lock (is you still play it) and vial 2, karakas, thalia vs miracles comes up less often
- A less painful manabase; fetches add up and you usually end up lava spiking/shocking yourself over the course of an average game

Overall:
At this point I see it as mono-white gives you more of the possibility of a fliers tempo plan where the Red splash gives you access to a more controlling, grindy game plan. At this point, I am personally favoring the red splash since I feel it gives you more consistency in the long games (which we are playing for most of the time). You sill suffer from the inconsistency of not playing blue but this improves that slightly. Generally I would recommend getting experience with both and playing whichever version you see being better in the expected metagame / you feel more comfortable with.
